## ⚠️ Option C as written does NOT close the gap — read this before implementing it

Two corrections to this card's premise. The first came from the dev who filed it, while writing the pin; the second follows from it and is mine.

### 1. It is not a round trip — the pointer is never stored at all

The pin's first version asserted the pointer was *stored, then lost on a round trip*. It failed: `expected undefined to be 'name'`. The strip runs on **every save**, so an author's redundant pointer is dropped by the **first write that carries it** — before any read, any `/meta` involvement, any round trip. There is nothing to lose because nothing is ever persisted.

Credit where due: the pin failed and the response was to re-derive the mechanism and correct the card, not to adjust the pin until it passed. The body above still describes the round-trip shape in places and should be read with this correction in front of it.

### 2. Therefore option C, as stated, is equivalent to option A on the case it exists to fix

C's rule is *strip only when redundant with the derivation **and** absent from the currently persisted row*. Walk the two scenarios:

| | stored row | incoming body | C's verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Phantom customisation** — author saved without a pointer, a read materialised one, client saves that body back | no pointer | redundant pointer | absent ⇒ **strip** ✅ correct |
| **The loss this card is about** — author deliberately writes `nameField: 'name'` on a fresh object | no pointer (nothing stored yet) | redundant pointer | absent ⇒ **strip** ❌ *same loss as A* |

C preserves a pointer only once it is already stored — and under A or C it can never *become* stored, so there is no state from which C's protection can ever engage. "Lossless in both directions" does not hold as written.

The underlying reason is worth stating plainly, because it is what makes this hard rather than fiddly: at the write boundary the two scenarios are **byte-identical in every field the platform can see** — same incoming pointer, same absent stored pointer. No comparison of body against stored row can separate them, because the difference is *provenance*, not content.

### What a taker should actually price

Do not implement C expecting it to work. The axis that carries real signal is **CREATE versus UPDATE**: on a create there is no prior read of this object to have injected anything, so a redundant pointer in a create body is author-written; the phantom-customisation path necessarily goes through a read first, and therefore an update. So the shape worth costing is roughly *do not strip on create; strip on update when absent from the stored row*.

That is not airtight either — a client can create from a template it read elsewhere — so the honest framing of this card is **"author-written and read-added are indistinguishable by content; here are the options and which harm each accepts"**, not "a lossless fix exists and here it is." Price CREATE/UPDATE, price a provenance mark, and price simply keeping A, before assuming a clean answer is available.

### What has not changed

The PM ruling stands: **A ships**. It remains observationally identical to C for every consumer — the resolved answer is the derivation's either way, `registerObject` re-derives on every boot, and the pin at `meta-object-primary-designation-roundtrip.test.ts` asserts both the unchanged resolved answer and that the read still serves it. This is a persistence-fidelity gap, not a behaviour regression, and option **B** stays ruled out (it bakes a read-added pointer into the tenant's row, checksum and history diffs — the #6562 phantom-customisation harm).

The fence note in the body is still correct and still worth reading: `saveMetaItem` was held by #8184, **#8184 has landed (`003feae65`)**, so whatever shape is chosen is immediately actionable.

## ESCALATE — `pm:queue` → `needs-user-decision`. The option in this card's title is measurably disproved, and what is left is a choice of which harm to accept.

PM session `session_01XeQRiAa7vYRVX5Fog7Zby8`, `domain:metadata` lane. Picked this up as the next dispatchable card after #8595 and #8608 landed; the pre-dispatch premise check stopped it. ⛔ Not claimed, no dev dispatched.

### Why it is not dispatchable as filed

The card's title prescribes **option C** ("make it stored-row-aware"). Comment `5279591027` — from the dev who filed it, while writing the pin — measured that C **does not close the gap**:

|  | stored row | incoming body | C's verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| phantom customisation | no pointer | redundant pointer | strip ✅ |
| **the loss this card is about** | no pointer (fresh object) | redundant pointer | strip ❌ **same as A** |

C protects a pointer only once it is *already stored*, and under either A or C it can never *become* stored — so there is no state from which C's protection can ever engage. Dispatching the card's own title would ship a change that does nothing for the case it names.

The reason is structural rather than fiddly, and it is why no clean answer is sitting here: **at the write boundary the two scenarios are byte-identical in every field the platform can see.** The difference is *provenance*, not content, so no comparison of body against stored row can separate them.

⚠️ Worth saying plainly: that correction exists because **the pin failed and the response was to re-derive the mechanism rather than adjust the pin until it passed.** The card body above still describes the round-trip shape in places and must be read with the correction in front of it.

### What is actually on the table

- **Keep A** (ships today). An author's explicit `nameField: 'name'` is dropped by the first write that carries it. Observationally identical for every consumer — the resolved answer is the derivation's either way, `registerObject` re-derives on every boot — so this is a **persistence-fidelity** gap, not a behaviour regression.
- **CREATE vs UPDATE.** On a create there is no prior read to have injected anything, so a redundant pointer in a create body is author-written; the phantom path necessarily goes through a read, hence an update. ⚠️ Not airtight — a client can create from a template it read elsewhere.
- **A provenance mark.** The only shape that separates the two by construction rather than by heuristic, and the only one that introduces new machinery to carry.
- ⛔ **Option B stays ruled out** — it bakes a read-added pointer into the tenant's row, checksum and history diffs (the #6562 phantom-customisation harm).

### Four-prism card face

1. **Platform long-term coherence** — a provenance mark is the only option that makes the distinction *expressible*; CREATE/UPDATE encodes a correlation the platform cannot actually verify, which is a special case that will need exceptions. Keeping A is coherent but leaves the declaration and the stored row permanently disagreeing.
2. **Measured business pull** — **thin, and stated honestly**: zero consumer-visible difference today. The harm is that an author writes something true and the platform silently discards it. No incident, no claimant. That argues against spending new machinery here and for either keeping A or waiting for pull.
3. **AI-agent error-resistance** — cuts both ways, which is why it does not settle it. Silently discarding an author's explicit declaration is the tolerant-consumer shape this repo keeps refusing; but baking a read-added pointer into a tenant's row (B) is the phantom-customisation shape it *also* refuses, and CREATE/UPDATE would do that on the template path.
4. **Startup scope discipline** — keeping A costs nothing. CREATE/UPDATE is small but not airtight. A provenance mark is real, permanent surface for a gap with no measured claimant.

### This seat's recommendation

**Keep A, and close or hold this card** — unless you want the provenance mark for its own sake. The measured pull is zero, the fidelity gap is invisible to every consumer, and both improvement options trade a silent discard for either an unverifiable heuristic or permanent new machinery. If it stays open, `pm:on-hold` with a named restart condition (a real author or agent reporting a lost declaration) is more honest than `pm:queue`, which is what it was carrying.

⛔ I have not closed or held it — that is your call, not this seat's. What I have changed is the state that said "ready to dispatch", because the option it prescribes was disproved on this very thread.

**Maintainer ruling** (delegated adjudication; delegation 2026-08-15 verbatim 「决策你直接帮我做」, batch confirmed 「同意」)

**Ruled: keep A (the shipped exactness-bounded strip). This card moves to `pm:on-hold` — not queued, not closed.**

The title's Option C is disproved on this thread by the filing dev's own measurement: the pointer is never persisted, so there is no stored state from which C's protection could ever engage — C is behaviourally identical to A on the exact case it was named for. At the write boundary the two scenarios are byte-identical; the difference is provenance, not content, so no content heuristic closes this. Option B stays ruled out (#6562 phantom-customisation harm). CREATE/UPDATE encodes a correlation the platform cannot verify (template-create path), and a provenance mark is permanent machinery for a gap with **zero measured pull** — no consumer-visible difference, no incident, no claimant.

**Restart condition, named**: a real author or agent reports a lost explicit `nameField` declaration (i.e. the fidelity gap acquires a claimant, e.g. a tier-outranking field is later added and a title silently moves where a stored pointer would have held it). On that report, reopen toward the provenance-mark direction — the only shape that separates the two cases by construction — and price it then.

Until then: A stands, the `MEASURES that an author pointer identical to the derivation does NOT survive` pin stays as the honest record of the divergence, and no dev is spent here.

Label flipped `needs-user-decision` → `pm:on-hold`.
